messages.author: 27ebba43052f7f0f
messages.subject: GSoC 2012 Project Proposal
parts:
Hello,

I'm Siddharth Kherada from International Institute of Information
Technology, Hyderabad, India. I am a MS by research student presently
working in the area of computer vision in the Center for Visual
Information Technology research center at IIIT-H. My areas of interest
are computer vision and machine learning. I would like to work for R
project for statistical computing in a GSoC project. I strongly
believe that this is going to be a good opportunity for me to work in
an Open Source Development society, related to my area of interest.
After going through R package I have found that there is a scope for
extending the Machine Learning Library by adding "Dimensionality
Reduction" algorithms in it. Since presently only few DR algos are
implemented like PCA, so I guess it could be a good addition to R
language.

Following is the list of algorithms that are being used extensively
for dimensionality reduction:

1.Locally Linear Embedding
2.Neighborhood Preserving Embedding
3.Kernel Locally Linear Embedding
4.Hessian Locally Linear Embedding
5.Local Tangent Space Alignment
6.Linear Local Tangent Space Alignment
7.Kernel Local Tangent Space Alignment
8.Laplacian Eigenmaps
9.Locality Preserving Projections
10.Diffusion Maps
11.Multidimensional Scaling
12.Isomap

Reference: http://homepage.tudelft.nl/19j49/Matlab_Toolbox_for_Dimensionality_Reduction.html

Most of this algorithms can be implemented from MATLAB to R.
I want to know your opinions about addition of these algorithms to R
and some other extensions to them.

Regards,
Siddharth Kherada
http://web.iiit.ac.in/~siddhartha_k/
http://siddharthkherada.tumblr.com/

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2012 Project Proposal - Dimension Reduction
parts:
Siddarth,

This looks like a very worthwhile set of functionality to port to R.

I definitely recommend that you apply.

The project you outline here in email is a good start, but I suggest
that you do a few additional things to help strengthen your
registration.

- demonstrate some R code from the project, perhaps port one of the
smaller functions, to demonstrate your coding capability

- add some design details to your application: what tasks do you think
need to happen to port this matlab code, what languages are required,
what challenges do you forsee?

- how do you plan to text or provide examples to demonstrate that the
ported functionality is correct?

- what other references can you provide to these methodologies?

- why did you choose only these methods? the toolbox has more.
have you considered other functionality from the library such
as the data generator or dimensionality extension, prewhitening,
or dimensionality estimation ?

Good Luck, and Regards,

- Brian

available in package pls.

And a few more technical questions in addition to Brian's "checklist":

Which package/system do you plan to use for:
- documentation
- version control
- Where do you plan to have the public repository?

Maybe I missed it, but how much experience do you have with R?

Best,

Claudia

messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2012 Project Proposal - Dimension Reduction
parts:
As regards the post on your blog -- I'm not entirely sure is(***,
"vector") does what you think it does:

E.g.,

x <- list( sin, "Margaret Thatcher", 1:5, NULL, NA, matrix(1:25, 5))
is(x, "vector") ## TRUE

You may be looking for is.numeric() instead.

Michael
